title: The Levee Love Affair Decades Later, Still Stormy: Confronting the Accreditation Crisis and Charting Solutions
content:
ABSTRACT

While levees safeguard over 23 million people and trillions of dollars in property, a profound, largely unrecognized flood risk crisis is emerging. Because approximately 75% of surveyed levees remain unaccredited, millions live behind levee systems that may not meet minimum federal safety standards. To overcome this accreditation bottleneck, this commentary translates research-driven opportunities into a prioritized, three-phase operational roadmap. First and most critically, regulators must transition from deterministic models to risk-based probabilistic frameworks that leverage economic indicators to guide local interventions. In the mid-term, engineering practices must integrate technical innovations, such as non-invasive geophysical field testing methods and artificial intelligence, alongside hybrid green-gray infrastructure solutions. Finally, achieving long-term resilience requires embedding transdisciplinary coproduction and design-centered alternatives into local governance. Ultimately, this framework moves beyond ‘check the box’ accreditation toward a holistic understanding of levee performance, equity, and community contexts, offering levee communities, management agencies, regulators, and researchers actionable pathways to safer, more resilient flood protection nationwide.
